# m12-slice-scoping

This directory holds the evidence and tooling for
[plan A](../../docs/plans/2026-09-27-slice-scoped-element-resolution.md) and
[plan B](../../docs/plans/2026-09-27-profile-false-negatives.md).

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `probes/` | Minimal instances, each isolating one defect. The plans' evidence tables name them. |
| `decisions/` | Instances for the plan A decisions (D-1 … D-6), with `hl7-6.10.4-output.txt`. |
| `packages/` | Invented (`acme`) FHIR packages. `acme.decisions` has differentials only, so its snapshots are generated by whichever validator loads it. |
| `hl7-validator-output*.json/txt` | Raw HL7 validator output for the probes, kept as evidence. It is not asserted directly. |
| `tools/sdparse.py`, `tools/r15.py` | StructureDefinition corpus parser (23 rules), plus the R15 refinement. Output: `tools/sdparse-corpus-2026-09-27.txt`. |
| `tools/gen_acme_decisions.py` | Regenerates `decisions/` and the `acme.decisions` package. |
| `corpus.json` | Regression corpus manifest for `hl7diff`. |
| `declared-divergences.json` | Message IDs where the spec wins over the HL7 validator (plan A, "Decisions"). |

## Checking the Release A invariant

Every error that is new relative to a baseline release must have an HL7 equivalent on the same
instance. Every error that disappears must be one that HL7 does not report.

```bash
go run ./internal/tools/hl7diff run \
  -manifest testdata/m12-slice-scoping/corpus.json \
  -jar /path/to/validator_cli.jar \
  -baseline v1.21.1            # default: latest tag
# -heavy     also run testdata/hl7-examples (5,310 files)
# -group a,b run only some groups
# -work dir  outputs and caches (default: $TMPDIR/gofhir-hl7diff)
```

The command builds `internal/tools/corpusrun` twice: from the working tree, and from a git worktree
of the baseline. It runs both builds and the HL7 validator on each group, then writes `report.md`.
HL7 output is cached per group, keyed by the jar, the FHIR version, the IGs and the file contents.
The exit status is 1 when any change is unjustified.

A group that cannot run (for example, because its packages are missing from `~/.fhir/packages`)
fails the run, since it proves nothing. Use `-group` to limit the run to the groups you can execute. The IG packages are
standard FHIR package `.tgz` files named `<id>#<version>.tgz`.
